pr.title: Star items and show only the starred ones

acceptance.evidence: migrations/0002_add_starred.sql adds starred NOT NULL DEFAULT 0 with CHECK; test 'AC-1' asserts all three rows are 0 and that a value of 2 is rejected.
test 'AC-2' checks the list is exactly [First item, ★ Second item, Third item].
test 'AC-3' stars 3 then 1 and asserts only the two starred items, in id order, with status 200.
test 'AC-4' checks both / and /?show=all give the full list in id order.

The spec's AC-5 now says the starred list links to 'Most items' (edited in d8e65cd). src/index.js renders 'All items' and test 'AC-5' asserts 'All items', so the code and test don't match the AC as written. The edit was made after the go with no recorded decision. The spec's States table and core flow still say 'All items'.
test 'AC-6' checks that Starred, none, an empty value and __proto__ each answer 400 with no <li>. The code uses Object.hasOwn.
traffic/routes.json contains '/?show=starred'. Test 'AC-7' asserts it, and tests/traffic-config.test.sh checks the checker accepts a query.

findings.what: Commit d8e65cd ('Follow-up edits', by a bot) changed AC-5's link label from 'All items' to 'Most items' after the go on 2026-10-12. No decision in the spec records the owner's call or its date. The PR says 'Changed after the go: nothing', which is false. The spec is also now inconsistent: the States table and Core flow still say 'All items'.
findings.fix: Revert the AC-5 edit, or get the owner's recorded decision with a date and make the code, test, States table and Core flow agree. Correct the PR's 'Changed after the go' line either way.

findings.what: The AC-5 test asserts 'All items', which contradicts the current AC-5 text ('Most items'). Under the spec as it stands, the implementation and its test are both wrong or the spec edit is wrong.
findings.fix: Resolve the spec wording first, then make the code and test follow it.

findings.what: 'Changed after the go: nothing' is false, because the spec's AC-5 was edited in a later commit. The PR also doesn't say that the traffic-config checker's validation was loosened beyond what the spec asks (queries now allowed for any route).
findings.fix: State the AC-5 edit and its status in the PR body.

lenses.note: The spec's intent is followed apart from the AC-5 label edit.
The States table has a test for each of its 4 rows. AC-5 was edited after the go with no recorded decision.
The tests assert behaviour and would fail on broken code. The AC-5 test conflicts with the current spec. I did not run the tests: they use the cloudflare workers pool and CI runs them.
The README mentions ?show=starred. The spec itself is internally inconsistent about the link label.
Whitelist lookup with Object.hasOwn, parameterised static SQL, and escaped titles. No defects found.
The show input is whitelisted and titles are HTML-escaped. No injection found. The only planted-instruction concern is the unattributed spec edit, reported under spec.
The page has only minimal HTML; no UI files such as CSS or components changed.
No browser flow or UI components in the diff beyond server-rendered markup.
The title is under 72 characters. 'Changed after the go: nothing' is false.
